newsitem.title: USA: Winds blamed for more southern Calif power outages.
newsitem.headline: Winds blamed for more southern Calif power outages.

text.p: Heavy winds in the Los Angeles area continued for a second day to cause scattered power outages, regional utilities said Tuesday.
"We are calling this our second worse storm in recent history," said Steve Conroy, spokesman for Edison International's Southern California Edison Co.
As of mid-day Tuesday, about 50 of Edison's transmission poles were knocked down by the strong winds, some blowing over 70 miles per hour, he noted.
The utility also had outages of several 220 kilovolt transmission lines, but no interstate lines were affected.
Most of the outages were due to falling trees and other debris knocking down local distribution lines.
Edison still had 50,000 customers without power by mid-Tuesday. "It could be a couple of days before everyone is back," said Conroy.
He noted that about one million customers have experienced outages ranging from a blinking of the lights to 24-hour outages during the wind storm.
